section_summary: This section documents U.S. monitoring and analysis of Japanese wartime radio. It includes Chungking Embassy correspondence about discontinuing routine broadcast summaries, an FBIS study of Radio Tokyo commentators and foreign-language propaganda personnel, and despatch no. 1445 compiling economic reports from Japanese and collaborationist broadcasts. The economic material emphasizes production, food supply, transport, communications, finance, and reconstruction in Japan and Japanese-occupied Asia, especially the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Department of State and OEW approval to discontinue Japanese-broadcast summaries
subfiles.from: Department of State and Office of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Approves the Embassy's request to stop sending mail and cable summaries of economic information from monitored Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: The Department and the Office of Economic Warfare concur with Chungking telegram no. 1374. The message authorizes discontinuance of the economic broadcast summaries and cites an August 13 telegram from Stone of OEW in its drafting notation.

subfiles.title: Draft message agreeing to discontinue broadcast summaries
subfiles.from: Department of State and Office of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Restates departmental and OEW agreement that the Embassy may cease its Japanese-broadcast summaries.
subfiles.summary: This short draft refers to Chungking's telegram no. 1374 of August 4. It repeats that both the Department and OEW agree to discontinuation of mail and cable summaries of economic material from monitored Japanese broadcasts.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 1374 requesting discontinuance of economic broadcast summaries
subfiles.about: Requests authority to end routine telegraphic and mail summaries of economic material from Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy argues that the Chinese Ministry of Information's releases are already sent by microfilm and that OWI's locally monitored English broadcasts are believed to duplicate FCC coverage. It offers weekly pouches of OWI Domei releases if OEW wants them, cites restrictions on secret-code use, and states that a final despatch covering July is being submitted.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram no. 1374
subfiles.about: Provides a security paraphrase of the Embassy's request to discontinue Japanese-broadcast summaries.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase gives the same three reasons as the received telegram: Ministry of Information microfilms, probable duplication by FCC of OWI monitoring, and limitations on secret-code use. It also records that the Embassy will send a despatch on July broadcasts because that material had already been translated and compiled.

subfiles.title: Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service Daily Report: Philippine Islands
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokyo broadcasts about an alleged guerrilla leader and Swiss residents in Manila.
subfiles.summary: One item reports the claimed capture of Lieutenant Colonel Hugh Straughn, previously called Hugh Strong, and labels him the instigator of an attempt against Laurel. A second item portrays Manila's Swiss community as politically aloof but economically helpful to the Japanese-sponsored “New Philippines,” while exploiting reports of Allied attacks for Axis propaganda.

subfiles.title: Letter thanking Goodwin Watson for the commentator study
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of an FBIS study of commentators and commentary on Japanese radio.
subfiles.summary: Salisbury thanks Watson for his August 14 letter and the enclosed study. He describes the study as interesting and useful to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of study on Tokyo's regular commentators
subfiles.from: Goodwin Watson, Chief, Analysis Division, Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service
subfiles.to: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Forwards an analytical study of Radio Tokyo's regular commentators and commentaries.
subfiles.summary: Watson sends the State Department a study prepared by the FBIS Far East Section. The letter serves as the cover for the report occupying the following pages.

subfiles.title: Tokyo's Regular Commentators and Commentaries
subfiles.from: Foreign Broadcast Intelligence Service, Analysis Division
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Profiles recurring English-language Radio Tokyo programs and the personnel of Japanese and Axis-controlled stations in Tokyo and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: The study evaluates the subjects, delivery, language, and propaganda effectiveness of Radio Tokyo commentators and programs, including “Light from the East,” “Women's Hour,” and the purported German relay. It then supplies biographical information on former Tokyo broadcasters and an extensive account of XGRS and other Shanghai stations. Particular attention is paid to American, Australian, Chinese, and European expatriates employed in Axis propaganda and to possible pseudonyms, loyalties, and broadcasting techniques.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding despatch no. 1445 and its Philippine excerpt
subfiles.to: K. D. Hester, Office of the U.S. High Commissioner, Department of the Interior
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of Chungking despatch no. 1445 and the portion of its enclosure concerning the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Lockhart sends Hester the August 7 Chungking despatch on Japanese economic broadcasts. He also encloses an excerpt containing the Philippine material for the Office of the High Commissioner.

subfiles.title: Copy of despatch no. 1445 with contents and Philippine excerpt
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., American Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Transmits selected July 1943 economic reports from Japanese broadcasts, followed here by the contents and the Philippine portion of the enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson explains that the reports were obtained from Chinese and American monitoring services in Chungking for the Office of Economic Warfare. The contents list economic items covering Japan and occupied Asia, while the reproduced excerpt reports postal and telegraph restoration, textile production, transportation, public works, revenues, banking, property restoration, remittances, and food substitutes in the Philippines. It closes with the beginning of the Netherlands East Indies section; page 30 is blank or illegible and functions as the package's final verso or separator.

subfiles.title: Enclosure no. 1 to despatch no. 1445: Economic items selected from Japanese and puppet-regime radio broadcasts
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Chungking, using Ministry of Information and OWI monitoring
subfiles.to: Department of State and Office of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Begins the full enclosure compiling July 1943 economic claims broadcast by Japan and collaborationist regimes.
subfiles.summary: After a multi-page table of contents, the enclosure explains that its reports were selected from Japanese- and Chinese-language monitoring and from English-language Domei material collected by OWI. The surviving pages cover Japanese aluminum and metal production, agricultural training, substitute soy sauce, iron-sand processing, irradiated grain, industrial mobilization, food shortages, rice crops, transport, labor, potato and tin controls, shipping-company mergers, fiber production, and rolling stock. The final page begins an item on a new military oil-filtering process and clearly continues beyond this section.
